The diffuse checker verifies 1584 translated endpoint formulas for five true prime pairs, including the centered displacement sums for cutoff and paired-deletion masks, sharp-selector identities and Bernstein convolution densities. It retains three true square controls at subfield orders 11, 19 and 43.

The terminal checker verifies the p=97 weighted source and genuine norm over the full evenized face, and the certified strict one-site erasure frontier across the full reflected faces at p=257 and p=409.

The forced checker reuses two earlier outward-rounded predictor records with exact rational arithmetic, then verifies the all-corank necessary RMS and two-orbit-deletion amplitude bounds. It does not assert an observed contact.
proof_scope: The short rational-prime shift family on each multiplicative translate divides the true marked cubic by two up to the stated mean absolute error. Strict disagreement pairs cancel positive and negative output counting terms exactly. Deleting both ends of every pair touched by a balanced R86 image preserves the corresponding comparison with the exact remaining centered cubic.

Bernstein convolution with actual point caps and threshold-averaged error gives a paired unweighted sharp diffuse cutoff on almost all thresholds in a shrinking window, simultaneously for all short translates. Complete-group estimates with different threshold ranges hold at every cutoff. All statements allow complex endpoint coefficients of ordinary theta. The short-family theorem fails on genuine square endpoints.

Height-weighted capacity V at a fixed-gap true terminal time gives both density and height cutoffs and a simultaneous erasure budget. With V=O_delta(d), order n/d sites retain comparable actual companion height through an order d/log^2(d) nearby window. The conditional high branch of a different weighted hinge implies p^(1/2-o(1)) inverse leverage, with common Jacobi head and both weighted and tower unweighted collision on the same surviving source.

At an actual finite enlarged-sector first contact on the height-600 real forcing path with q_*>0, any first noninteger exponent must be 1/2. Corank one gives a simple fold and a strictly smaller sign-definite side. The result at higher corank controls the first exponent only. Actual signed source projections depend on the transverse residual to every affine line.

The actual forced support ratio at most 3/2 requires q_* times the optimized amplitude-weighted transverse RMS above 1.89, or 3.12 at equal counts. Fitting a line through two amplitude outliers gives the necessary presence of at least three distinct active inversion orbits with amplitudes above 343/q_* or 567/q_*, respectively.

At every sufficiently large prime, alternating Fourier blocks yield even cross compression approaching one on a growing space and sets of size O(n/sqrt(log p)). The comparison factors preserve products, physical means, centered scalar pairings and bounded bulk amplitudes. This provides an obstruction to mask-only estimates, while leaving the genuine sector constraints to be used.
